ai_show_review.summary: Rare Lovelight jam with Cassady rap; only fragmentary recordings
ai_show_review.blurb: The available excerpts focus on an extended Lovelight performance that features a spoken Neil Cassady rap. The audience tape captures the jam with good clarity but fades before the end, while the soundboard fragment is only eight minutes and includes an early Lovelight snippet.
ai_show_review.review: On July 23, 1967 at San Francisco's Straight Theater the Dead slipped into an experimental zone that would later become legendary: a sprawling Lovelight rendition punctuated by Neil Cassady’s improvised rap. Unfortunately the show survives only in two incomplete recordings – a fair‑quality soundboard fragment that offers just an early glimpse of the song, and a good‑quality audience tape that stretches the jam out before cutting off abruptly. The audience capture is the more compelling listen, delivering a clearer mix and showcasing the band’s willingness to blend spoken word with music, even if it leaves us hanging before the conclusion. For collectors, these excerpts are valuable snapshots of an early Dead moment, but they don’t convey a full concert experience.

best_recording.reason: Good audience tape with extended Lovelight jam and clearer audio, despite ending early.

key_highlights: Extended Lovelight jam featuring a rare Neil Cassady spoken rap
Early fragment of Lovelight captured on soundboard
Both recordings are incomplete, offering only brief excerpts of the show
